zh.def: 請參與者帶一件物件或老照片，從「這件東西的故事」進入地方與家族記憶，而不是直接問大問題。
how: 請每人帶一件有故事的物件或老照片
用固定提問引導：這是誰的？什麼時候的？為什麼留著？
把口述錄下或寫下，連同物件一起保存
最後組成展覽、聲音導覽或一本小誌
zh.fit: 地方記憶、家族史、長者；對不擅長抽象表達的人特別友善。

en.def: Ask participants to bring an object or old photo and enter local and family memory through “the story of this thing”, instead of asking a big question head-on.
how: Each person brings one object or old photo with a story
Guide with set questions: whose is it? from when? why kept?
Record or write down the telling, and keep it with the object
Assemble the results into an exhibition, audio tour or zine
en.fit: Local memory, family history, elders; especially kind to people less at ease with abstraction.

zh.def: 把相機交給參與者，由他們決定拍什麼、希望外界怎麼認識自己。
how: 給一個開放的提問（例如「如果每月只有一天假」）
參與者自行拍攝，不規定主題
小組一起討論選片與下標題
展出時由拍攝者決定呈現與說法
zh.fit: 移工、少年、常被貼標籤的群體；核心是把話語權交給當事人。

en.def: Hand the camera to participants and let them decide what to shoot and how they want to be seen.
how: Pose one open question (e.g. ‘if you had one day off a month’)
Participants shoot on their own, with no set subject
Choose photos and write captions together in small groups
At the show, the photographer decides how it is presented
en.fit: Migrant workers, youth, often-labelled groups; the point is to hand narrative control to the people themselves.

zh.def: 不教表演，用戲劇遊戲與集體即興，讓居民把自己的生活編成戲。
how: 先用身體與信任的暖身遊戲破冰
田野採集居民的生活故事
用集體即興把故事發展成片段
不追求專業演出，重點在過程與關係
zh.fit: 社區、班級、跨世代；可容納素人與長者。

en.def: Don’t teach acting; use theatre games and collective improvisation so residents turn their own lives into a play.
how: Break the ice with body and trust warm-up games
Gather residents’ life stories through fieldwork
Develop the stories into scenes by collective improvisation
Don’t chase a professional show; the process and relationships matter most
en.fit: Communities, classes, across generations; room for non-professionals and elders.

zh.def: 用錄音把一個地方或一群工作者的聲音收集起來，做成聲音故事或語音導覽。
how: 選定對象：攤商、工作者或一段地景
訪談或現場收音
剪成幾分鐘內的短聲音故事
用耳機或語音導覽讓人在真實空間裡聆聽
zh.fit: 勞動、地方記憶；適合不想露臉的參與者。

en.def: Use recording to gather the sounds of a place or a group of workers into sound stories or an audio tour.
how: Pick a subject: vendors, workers, or a stretch of landscape
Interview or record on site
Edit into short sound stories of a few minutes
Let people listen in the real space through headphones or an audio guide
en.fit: Labour, local memory; suits participants who would rather not be seen.

zh.n: 在地素材與廢棄物再製
zh.def: 用在地或被丟棄的材料（漁網、漂流木、海廢、舊布條）創作，讓材料本身承載議題。
how: 一起蒐集材料：淨灘、撿拾或向社區徵集
認識材料的來歷與它背後的問題
動手改造成作品
展示時連結材料的來源故事
zh.fit: 環境、社區；讓行動（淨灘）與創作合而為一。

en.def: Make work from local or discarded materials — fishing nets, driftwood, marine debris, old banners — so the material itself carries the issue.
how: Gather materials together: beach cleanups, scavenging, or a community call
Learn where the material came from and the problem behind it
Remake it into a work by hand
Link the display back to the material’s origin story
en.fit: Environment, community; fuses action (a cleanup) with creation.

zh.n: 走讀、地圖與感知資料庫
zh.def: 帶參與者實地走讀一個地方，用地圖、學習單或蓋章存檔把觀察收集起來。
how: 設計走讀路線與一份《探索筆記》
邊走邊記錄：照片、聲音、訪談
把成果匯整成地圖或資料庫
回饋給社區，成為公共的資料
zh.fit: 地方認識、都市變遷；適合親子與學生。

en.def: Take participants on a field walk and gather their observations with maps, worksheets or a stamp-and-file system.
how: Design a walking route and an ‘exploration notebook’
Record while walking: photos, sound, interviews
Compile the results into a map or database
Give it back to the community as a public resource
en.fit: Getting to know a place, urban change; good for families and students.

zh.n: 以現成文件與文物當提問起點
zh.def: 從一份真實的歷史文件、館藏或文物出發，讓大問題從具體的物件長出來，而不是老師先定題目。
how: 選一件有張力的文件或文物（一句話、一幅畫、一件文物）
用它向參與者拋問，而不是給答案
讓參與者接著發展自己的回應與創作
把個人創作連回那份文件的脈絡
zh.fit: 歷史、認同、美感教育；是「議題從脈絡浮現」的關鍵技巧。

en.def: Start from a real historical document, collection or artefact, letting the big question grow from a concrete object rather than a teacher-set topic.
how: Pick a charged document or artefact (a single line, a painting, an object)
Use it to pose a question, not to give an answer
Let participants develop their own responses and work
Tie the personal work back to the document’s context
en.fit: History, identity, aesthetic education; the key move for letting issues emerge from context.

zh.def: 刻意讓不同世代（長者與學生、舞者）同組創作，讓記憶與技藝在互動中傳遞。
how: 把不同世代配成一組
設計需要彼此的任務：長者口述、年輕人記錄或編創
一起排練、同台發表
讓雙方都被看見，而不只是長者被訪問
zh.fit: 地方記憶、客庄與族群文化；長照與樂齡場域。

en.def: Deliberately put different generations — elders with students or dancers — in the same group, so memory and skills pass on through interaction.
how: Pair up across generations
Design tasks that need each other: elders tell, younger ones record or choreograph
Rehearse and present on stage together
Make sure both sides are seen, not just the elder interviewed
en.fit: Local memory, Hakka and ethnic cultures; care-station and senior settings.

zh.n: 在歷史現場與軍事遺構裡創作
zh.def: 不把歷史現場當背景看板，而是直接在防空洞、碉堡、眷村、老屋裡創作或展演，讓空間本身成為教材與媒材；這是限地製作（site-specific）用在記憶場域教學的一種應用。
how: 選一處有張力、仍保有痕跡的現場（碉堡、防空洞、眷村、廢墟）
先帶參與者用身體與感官認識這個空間：走、聽、觸、記錄
從空間的用途與歷史拋問，而不是先講解牌式地給答案
讓作品或展演留在原地發生，而非搬到展間；必要時結合在地媒材
zh.fit: 地方史、冷戰與戰地記憶、文資活化；把抽象歷史變成可被身體經驗的現場。

en.n: Working inside historical sites and military remains
en.def: Don’t treat the historical site as a backdrop; create or perform straight inside bomb shelters, bunkers, villages and old houses, so the space itself becomes both lesson and material; it is one educational application of site-specific art to memory-laden places.
how: Pick a charged site that still bears its traces (bunker, bomb shelter, village, ruin)
First have participants know the space through body and senses: walk, listen, touch, record
Pose questions from the site’s use and history, rather than giving wall-label answers
Let the work or performance happen in place, not moved to a gallery; bring in local materials where it fits
en.fit: Local history, Cold-War and battlefield memory, heritage activation; turns abstract history into something the body can experience on site.

zh.n: 共食共作：以餐桌與食物凝聚關係
zh.def: 先不急著創作，用一起吃飯、交換食譜、共同備餐等飲食活動當媒介，讓參與者先建立關係與信任，關係成熟後再長出作品。
how: 固定節奏的共餐或共同備餐（例如每月一次『一家一菜』）
用食物交換引出個人故事：換食譜就是換記憶、換家鄉
先累積關係與信任，不要第一次就談創作
關係成熟後再導入共創，並把餐桌經驗轉成作品或刊物
zh.fit: 社宅、社區、長照與跨文化等『需要先交陪』的場域；對陌生、異質或流動的住民特別有效。

en.def: Don’t rush to make art; use shared meals, recipe-swaps and cooking together as the medium, letting participants build relationships and trust first, and let the work grow once the relationships are there.
how: Hold regular shared meals or cook-togethers (e.g. a monthly potluck)
Use food exchange to draw out personal stories: swapping recipes swaps memories and homelands
Build relationship and trust first — don’t talk about ‘creating’ at the first meal
Bring in co-creation once the relationships are there, and turn the table into a work or a zine
en.fit: Social housing, communities, elder care and cross-cultural settings that need trust first; especially good for unfamiliar, mixed or transient residents.

zh.n: 在地職人與耆老當老師：以活工藝共作
zh.def: 刻意翻轉師生角色，請社區裡的匠師與耆老當老師，帶參與者以在地仍活著的工藝技藝（編織、染、陶、糊紙等）共同創作。
how: 先在社區裡找到還在做的匠師或耆老，請他們當老師
由職人示範並帶領在地技藝（編織、植物染、陶、糊紙等）
參與者動手學，再一起把技藝用到共同作品上
把成果連回這項技藝的來歷與傳承脈絡
zh.fit: 原住民族與客庄文化、傳統工藝活化；讓在地知識被看見、也被傳下去。（與『在地素材再製』『跨世代共作』部分重疊，差別在這裡以『職人為師、活的技藝』為核心。）

en.n: Local masters and elders as teachers
en.def: Deliberately invert the teacher–student roles: invite the community’s craftspeople and elders to teach, and co-create with participants through living local crafts (weaving, dyeing, ceramics, paper-craft, etc.).
how: Find craftspeople or elders in the community who still practise, and invite them to teach
Have the masters demonstrate and lead a living local craft (weaving, plant-dyeing, ceramics, paper-craft…)
Participants learn hands-on, then put the craft to work on a shared piece
Tie the result back to the craft’s origins and its line of transmission
en.fit: Indigenous and Hakka cultures, reviving traditional crafts; lets local knowledge be seen and passed on. (Overlaps partly with found-material making and cross-generational co-creation; the difference is its focus on masters-as-teachers and living skills.)
